title: Sukha Singh Is Betrayed at Home and Jumps Into a Well

blocks.text: Sukha Singh avoids his home because Mughal surveillance makes family space dangerous. His parents, however, try to reclaim him from the Panth by arguing that their household has no place in Sikh sovereignty and by treating his Khalsa commitment as a dishonor to caste expectations.

Their deception culminates in intoxicating him and cutting his hair. When he awakens to that violation, his grief is so fierce that he refuses ordinary consolation and jumped into a deep well rather than continue under disgrace.

The page therefore frames the crisis as spiritual betrayal rather than domestic conflict alone. What has been attacked is not merely Sukha Singh's appearance, but the covenantal identity by which he belongs to the Khalsa.
